chapter: Opening and the New York trip
title: Ragtime, 'ratty' bands and the Original Dixieland players
summary: The music was called ragtime, and some would not hire a 'ratty band'; Garland says the Original Dixieland band came after him and he knew Spargo, Shields, LaRocca and others from New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And I just wondered, because I didn't know much about jazz in New York in those early days, and, you know, New Orleans music, anyway, I'll call it.
Well, at that time, they said the only jazz band.
Yeah. But they used to say something else before that. Mm-hmm. Didn't they? Yeah. What did they say? What words did they have for the music when you were coming up?
Well, before my time, they used to call it ratty music. Did you ever hear that?
Yeah. A lot of people wouldn't hire us. They'd say they want that ratty band.
That's right. Was the original Dixieland jazz band in New York when you were there, do you think? No. Because they were there just before the Lord. You knew that guy they called?
Oh, you knew the Red? Red Nichols, you mean? No, no.
No. No. What was his name? Monkey?
That's the drummer. Yeah. What did you call him? You called him Monkey, huh? Spargo. Spargo.
Tony. Mm-hmm. Did you know Harry Shields and Eddie Edwards and all those? Sure.
Nick LaRocco? I knew all them guys.
Oh, yeah? Did they follow you around when they were youngsters?
In the Orleans, yeah. You know, I can't think I'm in the Orleans.
